observations: Photo 0 shows a disassembled automatic transmission valve body with a black electronic control module (ECM) attached.
Photo 1 shows the same valve body with a hand using a tool on the top surface.
Photo 2 shows the valve body with a long metal rod inserted into the input shaft.
The valve body has a complex internal structure with multiple ports and solenoid connectors.
The ECM is secured with a black rubber grommet.
The surrounding area contains other transmission components and fluid containers.

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1, and 2 show the valve body with all internal components and the attached ECM.
No part number, casting number, or Hyundai branding is visible in the photos.

risks.risk: The valve body may be a generic or third-party part rather than a genuine Hyundai component.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the part number stamped on the valve body casing.

risks.risk: The electronic control module (ECM) may be faulty or have a damaged connector.
risks.proof: A video showing the ECM being powered on and communicating with a diagnostic tool.

risks.risk: Internal seals or gaskets may be missing or damaged.
risks.proof: A photo of the valve body with all seals and gaskets installed.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the part number stamped on the valve body casing.
Photo of the valve body with all seals and gaskets installed.
Video of the ECM being tested with a diagnostic tool.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
